# Synthetic comparison result

## Outcome

C1 does not meet the promotion rule. Its error is higher than B0, and the gain is −0.03 absolute error units, below the required +0.01.

This finding assesses the organization increment after both arms receive the same records. Retain B0 within this fictional comparison.

## Evidence

The supplied [metrics](evidence/metrics.json) mark the observations as synthetic and error as lower-is-better: B0 = 0.20, C1 = 0.23, minimum gain = 0.01. [Derived evidence](evidence/derived.json) correctly records 0.20 − 0.23 = −0.03 and promote = false. The accepted [arithmetic check](check_arithmetic.py) checks the gain and promotion label during managed verification.

The [governing question](../../research/questions/Q.md#mechanism) and related [organization-only route](../../research/ROUTES.md#organization-only-comparison) identify the same-records boundary. The evidence supports the decision to decline C1 promotion under the fixed rule; the broader component-complementarity question remains unanswered.

## Deviations

None in the specified synthetic assessment; the threshold and inputs are unchanged.

## Next action

Retain B0 within this fictional comparison and close the assessment after both required checks pass. There is no authorized extra experiment.

## Limitations

All observations are synthetic aggregates. They establish no real model performance, prediction quality, uncertainty, or general scientific conclusion. This organization-only comparison does not isolate complementary components and neither supports nor refutes whether combining complementary logical components improves generated programs.

---
name: research-task
description: Manage bounded rctl research tasks, resume their handoffs, verify or close them, initialize research workspaces, and plan related experiments.
---

# Research task

Orient selected work using a fresh `rctl status TASK` or delivered reminder. Follow
its source paths for criteria, warnings, and missing or truncated details. The
retained contract owns the accepted agreement; `state.md` reports progress and
`result.md` interprets evidence. The machine record owns verification and phase.

Use the relevant reference when entering an operation:

| Operation | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Initialize, inspect/update installation, use a vault, or migrate | [Workspace](references/workspace.md) |
| Author contract, result, review input, or handoff | [Task files and examples](references/task-files.md) |
| Propose an experiment, create its contract, or materially change scientific direction | [Planning and history reuse](references/planning.md) |
| Evaluate evidence, verify, or close | [Verification and closeout](references/verification.md) |

Before experimental planning, cite related history, what remains unanswered, and
which decision new evidence changes. For a task derived from a broader question,
use the optional Question alignment fields in the task-file reference and keep
conclusions within `This task tests` and `This task does not decide`.

Fill the agreement and acceptance criteria before `begin`. Choose methods and order
within existing authorization; preparing a contract does not require another approval.
Use domain skills for scientific methods and evidence, and rctl for this task's
lifecycle. Advice and bounded mechanical edits may stay inline without a managed task.

## Commands and addressing

`TASK` is an explicit project-relative path, such as `tasks/retained-check`.
Global options precede the command: `rctl --root /absolute/project --format json status TASK`.
JSON results are under `data`, beside `ok`, `error`, and `warnings`.

| Intent | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Find work | `rctl task list --phase active` (omit the filter for all phases) |
| Read state | `rctl --format json status TASK` |
| Refresh reminder | `rctl context [TASK]` |
| Create draft | `rctl task new TASK --kind analysis --title "Bounded question"` |
| Check structure | `rctl contract check TASK` |
| Retain agreement | `rctl begin TASK` |
| Accept changed agreement | `rctl amend TASK --reason "Why it changed"` |
| Save handoff | `rctl checkpoint TASK --file .work/handoff.md` |
| Verify | `rctl verify TASK --reviews TASK/reviews.json` (omit reviews for command-only tasks) |
| Close | `rctl close TASK` |
| Resume an ended task | `rctl reopen TASK --reason "Why work resumes"` |
| Stop without closure | `rctl cancel TASK --reason "Why work stops"` |

Root selection is `--root`, then `RCTL_PROJECT_ROOT`, then the working directory.
Listing never selects a task. `RCTL_TASK_PATH` supplies an omitted task only for
context/hooks; lifecycle commands require `TASK`. CLI `--file` and `--reviews`
paths resolve from the project root; document `evidence_refs`, command `inputs`,
and command execution resolve from the task directory. Use targeted help for
unfamiliar syntax or version differences; reuse established syntax otherwise.

## Completion and handoff

Managed completion requires successful `close` with a current passing verification.
A negative or bounded inconclusive scientific result can satisfy that agreement.
Structural checks establish structure; execution and inspected evidence support a
claim. A nonzero `verify` may still save a report; inspect status after an uncertain
write before continuing.

To pause, checkpoint a handoff with `## Next action` and `## Blockers` first and one
concrete continuation step. Reported handoff progress is separate from lifecycle
advice. A chat ending does not close the task. Use uv for Python setup and execution.
# Native task files

Use these examples when authoring a contract, result, or review input. They form a
synthetic `tasks/retained-check` task, not evidence for a live research conclusion.
Replace the question, criteria, evidence, and judgments with the actual agreement.
Keep the task ID generated by `task new`; obtain the current contract revision from
`rctl --format json status TASK` under `data.contract_revision`.

## Contract: `contract.md`

`task new` creates this file only. Fill its frontmatter and all four required
sections before `contract check` and `begin`. Every criterion is required.

```markdown
---
schema_version: 1
task_id: retained-check
title: Inspect a retained count summary
kind: analysis
criteria:
  - id: AC-01
    requirement: The retained counts sum to the reported total.
    evidence_refs: [evidence/counts.json]
    failure_action: Correct the summary against its source or leave the task unresolved.
    method:
      type: command
      argv: [uv, run, --no-project, --script, check_counts.py]
      timeout_seconds: 30
      inputs: [check_counts.py, evidence/counts.json]
  - id: AC-02
    requirement: The result limits its claim to arithmetic consistency of supplied counts.
    evidence_refs: [result.md, evidence/counts.json]
    failure_action: Narrow the result to what the retained evidence supports.
    method:
      type: review
      reviewer: either
---

## Question

- Question: Is the supplied count summary internally consistent?
- Origin and related history: Supplied arithmetic fixture; no related experiment history.

## Scope

Inspect the retained summary and its arithmetic only.

## Constraints

Use existing local evidence. No new data collection, remote jobs, or source-data audit.

## Stop conditions

Stop after one inspection and verification. Report inconsistent counts honestly;
do not regenerate evidence to manufacture a passing check.
```

For an experimental proposal, expand Question/Scope with the history actually inspected.
For example: a cited route tested an intervention only at one fixed budget; the proposed
comparison would test a different objective against an equal-compute control, satisfying
that route's stated reopen condition. Name the unresolved mechanism and the decision
that each possible result changes. This arithmetic-only example needs no invented route.

When the experiment isolates one relationship inside an existing project question,
add the optional section below after `## Question`:

```markdown
## Question alignment

- Governing question source: research/questions/C15.md#mechanism
- Governing mechanism: Complementary logical components may improve generated programs when combined.
- This task tests: The organization increment after both arms receive the same records.
- This task does not decide: Whether the broader cross-candidate mechanism is supported.
```

Use the actual readable project-relative Markdown source and an optional fragment;
keep each declared relationship field to one short sentence.
If present, all four fields must be nonempty and no extra prose or fields belong in
the section. `contract check` establishes structure and source availability only.
When scientific adequacy of the relationship affects closure, add a review criterion
whose evidence includes that source file and `result.md`; `evidence_refs` still
resolve from the task directory, so use the corresponding task-relative path without
the fragment (for example, `../../research/questions/C15.md` from `tasks/TASK`). The
review must decide whether the result stays within the declared test and non-claim
boundary.

For command checks, `argv` is an argument array executed without a shell, with the
task directory as cwd. Declare the checker, helper files, and preexisting data in
`inputs`. A check validates available evidence; generate analysis outputs before
`verify`, since changing declared evidence during verification prevents a pass.

For this disposable example, supply `evidence/counts.json`:

```json
{"counts": [2, 3], "total": 5}
```

And task-local `check_counts.py`:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path

summary = json.loads(Path("evidence/counts.json").read_text())
if sum(summary["counts"]) != summary["total"]:
    raise SystemExit("Retained counts do not match the total.")
print("Retained counts match the total.")
```

Command exit zero establishes this arithmetic check only. The second criterion
requires an evidence-based judgment of the result's claim.

## Result: `result.md`

Create this file after inspecting evidence. Use the current revision and all five
required sections. `assessment` is one of `supported`, `not_supported`,
`inconclusive`, or `not_applicable`; it is separate from phase and check verdict.

```markdown
---
schema_version: 1
task_id: retained-check
contract_revision: 1
assessment: supported
---

## Outcome

The supplied counts are internally consistent: 2 + 3 = 5.

## Evidence

Inspected evidence/counts.json, which contains counts [2, 3] and total 5.
check_counts.py checks this arithmetic during verification.

## Deviations

None.

## Next action

Verify the declared criteria, then close if the current report passes.

## Limitations

Internal consistency does not establish that the counts match the source data.
```

## Review input: `reviews.json`

Write entries after inspecting the cited content. Include only review criteria,
using their exact IDs and all their required evidence references. The top-level
array is `checks`. Each `verdict` is `pass`, `fail`, or `unknown`; each `reviewer`
is `agent` or `operator`. A contract's `reviewer: operator` needs an actual operator
judgment; `either` permits either source. Record missing judgments as unresolved.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "task_id": "retained-check",
  "contract_revision": 1,
  "checks": [
    {
      "criterion_id": "AC-02",
      "verdict": "pass",
      "reviewer": "agent",
      "rationale": "The result reports 2 + 3 = 5 from the supplied JSON and explicitly excludes source-data validity.",
      "evidence_refs": ["result.md", "evidence/counts.json"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Run `rctl verify tasks/retained-check --reviews tasks/retained-check/reviews.json`
from the project root. In JSON mode, inspect `data.verdict`, `data.checks`, and
`error`; a nonzero exit can still save a report. Use `status` after an uncertain
write. Address the named failure before another verification; a changed contract
requires `amend`, with result/review revision numbers updated accordingly.

## Handoff: `state.md`

Prepare a separate UTF-8 file, such as `.work/handoff.md`, then save it using
`rctl checkpoint TASK --file .work/handoff.md`. Use the actual next step:

```markdown
## Next action

Inspect result.md against evidence/counts.json and write the AC-02 review.

## Blockers

None.

## Progress

The contract is active; the retained evidence and result are ready for review.
```

Handoff updates preserve verification applicability. Contract amendments, result
or evidence changes, and reopened cycles require fresh verification before close.
# Verification and closeout

Use the current agreement's criteria and [Task files](task-files.md) when preparing
the result and reviews. Generate analysis artifacts before verification; declared
local checks validate existing evidence. Include check scripts, helpers, and
preexisting data in command inputs. New remote jobs need their own authority.

Write the current revision's result with outcome, evidence, deviations, next action,
and limitations. Distinguish computed observations, parsed evidence, and hypotheses.
For an aligned task, assess only the declared test and honor its non-claim scope.
Inspect cited content before supplying a review verdict, reviewer source, rationale,
and all required references. An operator-only criterion needs an operator judgment;
reviewer labels are declared sources, not authenticated identities.

Run `rctl verify TASK --reviews FILE`, omitting reviews for command-only criteria.
Inspect every criterion and its logs as needed. Nonzero verification can still save
a report; use status after an interruption or uncertain write. Correct the named
failure within the agreement or leave work unresolved, then explicitly verify again.
Changed results/evidence, amendments, and reopened cycles require fresh verification.
An unfavorable finding does not justify expanding the budget or weakening criteria.

Close only when the latest report passes and remains applicable. Scientific
`not_supported` and bounded `inconclusive` results can close. A missing judgment or
unknown check remains unresolved; an older pass cannot replace a later failed report.
`reopen --reason TEXT` starts a new cycle; `cancel --reason TEXT` stops active work
without verified completion.

Promote established findings to existing project research files at closeout, keeping
their scope and evidence links. Task progress and execution history remain with the
task. To pause instead, checkpoint a concrete next action, blockers, last verified
progress, evidence locations, and unresolved work. The source handoff preserves the
detail that a bounded reminder may omit.
